definition_zh: 也许；可能地；（与 can、could 连用）究竟；能否
definition_en: perhaps; used with can or could to stress surprise or doubt, or to make a request sound polite
core_image: 一盏忽明忽暗的灯：会不会亮，此刻还说不准
scene: 朋友问周末要不要去爬山，她看了看窗外的乌云，没有马上答应。 The sky may possibly clear up by Saturday morning.
sceneCN: 这里是「也许」（第 1 个义项：表示不确定）；句意为到周六早上天色也许会放晴。画面可留意的是窗外压低的云和那盏还没开的灯。

pos.zh: 也许；可能地；（用于强调或委婉请求）

derivatives.zh: possibly 加否定前缀 im- 构成，表示「不可能地；难以想象地」
possibly 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，表示「可能的」
同一词族的名词形式，表示「可能性」

senses.title: Perhaps; it may be so
senses.definition: used to say that something may be true or may happen, but is not certain
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事也许是真的，或者也许会发生，但并不确定
senses.example: She will possibly arrive before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 她也许中午前会到。
senses.why: The adverb carries the adjective's sense of ability into a judgement the speaker will not fully commit to.
senses.whyCN: 副词把形容词「能够」的意思带进一句说话人不敢完全担保的判断里，说的就是「也许」。

senses.title: Used with can or could for emphasis
senses.definition: used after can or could to show surprise, doubt or strong feeling about whether something is possible
senses.definitionCN: 用在 can 或 could 之后，对某事是否可能表示惊讶、怀疑或强烈语气
senses.example: How could she possibly forget the keys again?
senses.exampleCN: 她怎么可能又把钥匙忘了？
senses.why: If ability is stressed to its limit, a neutral question turns into a challenge to belief.
senses.whyCN: 把「能力」强调到极限，原本中性的问句就变成了对「这怎么可能」的质疑。

senses.title: Used to make a polite request
senses.definition: used in questions such as could you possibly to make a request sound careful and polite
senses.definitionCN: 用于 could you possibly 这类问句，使请求显得客气、留有余地
senses.example: Could you possibly send me the file today?
senses.exampleCN: 您今天能不能把文件发给我？
senses.why: Asking whether someone even has the ability to help softens the demand and leaves an easy way to refuse.
senses.whyCN: 先问对方「有没有可能帮上」，请求就变软了，也给对方留了容易拒绝的余地。

intro.en: Possibly is the adverb of possible, and both go back to the Latin verb posse, to be able.
intro.cn: possibly 是 possible 的副词，两者都追溯到拉丁语动词 posse（能够）。

items.en: Potis, an old Latin adjective for able or powerful, combined with esse, to be, to yield the verb of ability.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 potis 表示「有能力的、有力量的」，它与 esse（是）结合，产生了表示「能够」的动词。

items.en: Posse meant to be able, and from it Latin built possibilis, that which can be done.
items.cn: posse 意为「能够」，拉丁语由它造出 possibilis，即「做得到的」。

items.en: Old French used possible for what can be or can happen, and English borrowed the adjective in this form.
items.cn: 古法语用 possible 表示「能够存在或发生的」，英语以这个形式借入了形容词。

items.en: Middle English possible described what is within reach or within reason, close to its modern meaning.
items.cn: 中古英语的 possible 指「做得到、说得通」的事，与现代义已经很接近。

items.en: English added the adverb ending -ly to the adjective, giving possibly, which marks an unsure judgement rather than an ability.
items.cn: 英语给这个形容词加上副词词尾 -ly，造出 possibly，用来标记没有把握的判断，而不是单纯的能力。

note.en: The first group follows the same Latin stem through its adjective, negative and noun forms; the second follows the meaning of uncertainty.
note.cn: 形近组沿同一拉丁词干看它的形容词、否定式与名词形式；近义组则沿「不确定」这条意义线展开。

entries.definition: The adjective that possibly is built from, meaning able to be or happen.
entries.definitionCN: possibly 所由构成的形容词，意为「可能的」。

entries.definition: Not able to happen or be done, with the negative prefix im-.
entries.definitionCN: 加否定前缀 im-，意为「不可能的」。

entries.definition: The noun naming the chance that something may be or happen.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事可能存在或发生的「可能性」的名词。

entries.definition: The negative adverb, used of things too difficult to imagine.
entries.definitionCN: 否定副词，用于难以想象地困难的事物。

entries.definition: A neutral word for maybe, common in careful speech.
entries.definitionCN: 中性的「也许」，在谨慎的表述中很常见。

entries.definition: A plainer, more conversational way to say perhaps.
entries.definitionCN: 更口语、更朴素的「也许」。

entries.definition: More likely than not, a stronger claim than possibly.
entries.definitionCN: 多半如此，语气比 possibly 更肯定。

entries.definition: In a way that can be imagined, however slight the chance.
entries.definitionCN: 在可以想象的范围内，不论机会多小。

normalIntro.en: The word is an adjective of ability turned into an adverb, so its endings carry most of its history.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示「能够」的形容词转为副词，它的历史大半写在词尾上。

normal.en: Possibly is possible plus -ly, the ordinary English way of turning an adjective into an adverb.
normal.cn: possibly 就是 possible 加 -ly，这是英语把形容词变成副词最普通的方式。

normal.en: The -ly ending adds no doubt of its own; the uncertainty already sits inside possible.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 本身并不带来怀疑，不确定早就藏在 possible 里。

normal.en: Impossibly adds im- to possibly and closes the door: not even able to be imagined.
normal.cn: impossibly 在 possibly 前加 im-，把门关死，意为「连想都不可能」。

normal.en: In could you possibly, the adverb stretches ability into politeness rather than doubt.
normal.cn: 在 could you possibly 里，这个副词把「能力」拉长成客气，而不是怀疑。

normal.en: The double s in the spelling marks the Latin stem pos-se, which also shows in possible and impossible.
normal.cn: 拼写里的双写 s 标出拉丁词干 pos-se，在 possible 与 impossible 里同样出现。

abstract.en: Possibly is the word for leaving a door ajar without promising to walk through it.
abstract.cn: possibly 是「把门留着缝，却不保证走进去」时用的词。

abstract.en: A forecast lives on possibly: it names a chance rather than a fact.
abstract.cn: 天气预报就活在 possibly 上：它给的是机会，不是事实。

abstract.en: Saying possibly moves the weight of proof away from the speaker and onto the future.
abstract.cn: 说 possibly，就把举证的分量从说话人身上推给了未来。

examples.en: The meeting will possibly be moved to Thursday.
examples.cn: 会议也许会被改到周四。

examples.en: Could you possibly lend me your notes?
examples.cn: 你能不能把笔记借给我？

examples.en: She is possibly the best player on the team.
examples.cn: 她也许是队里最好的球员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕谁不力」——怕谁不肯出力，事情就只能说「也许」；记住 possibly 表示可能地。

root: possibly 由 possible 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，词干回到拉丁语 posse（能够）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an unsure maybe; the same adverb then hardens into emphatic disbelief and softens into a polite request.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是不确定的「也许」；同一个副词既能加重成质疑，也能放软成客气的请求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp that flickers, so nobody can say yet whether the room will be lit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏忽明忽暗的灯，房间会不会亮起来，此刻没人说得准。

branches.en: a forecast that keeps changing its mind
branches.cn: 一份反复改口的预报

branches.en: a friend asking how such a thing could ever happen
branches.cn: 朋友追问这种事怎么可能发生

branches.en: a carefully worded request left open to refusal
branches.cn: 一句留好退路的请求

branches.en: a rumour that nobody can confirm
branches.cn: 一则没人能证实的传闻

branches.en: a question mark placed before a favour
branches.cn: 在请求前放一个问号

intro.en: The word is an adjective of ability plus the English adverb ending, and its family adds a negative prefix and a noun suffix around the same Latin stem.
intro.cn: 这个词是「能够」的形容词加英语副词词尾构成，词族在同一拉丁词干周围再加否定前缀与名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin posse and possibilis carry the core meaning; the English adverb ending does the grammatical work.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 posse 与 possibilis 承载核心意义，英语副词词尾负责语法功能。

definition_en: to feel sorry about something one has done or failed to do; a feeling of sorrow over what cannot be changed; a polite refusal
core_image: 一封没有寄出的信被反复拿起又放回抽屉
scene: 抽屉里有一封始终没有寄出的信，他反复拿起来，又放回去。 He regretted the words as soon as they left his mouth.
sceneCN: 这里 regretted 是 regret 的过去式，取「后悔」（第 1 个义项：为自己做过的事感到懊悔）；句意为话一出口他就后悔了。画面里可留意：被反复拿起又放回的信。

derivatives.zh: 懊悔的；遗憾的
令人遗憾的
遗憾的是

senses.title: To feel sorry for one's act
senses.definition: to wish one had not done something one did
senses.definitionCN: 希望自己没有做过某件已做的事
senses.example: He regretted the words as soon as they left his mouth.
senses.exampleCN: 话一出口他就后悔了。
senses.why: The word is a looking back with sorrow: the mind turns to a past act and finds it painful to hold.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「带着悲伤的回望」：心思转向过去的某个举动，发现它难以承受。

senses.title: Sorrow over what cannot change
senses.definition: to feel sad about a fact or a loss that one cannot alter
senses.definitionCN: 对无法改变的事实或失去感到难过
senses.example: We regret that the museum will close for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆冬季将闭馆，我们对此感到遗憾。
senses.why: When the past act is not one's own, the same sorrow becomes a formal expression of sympathy.
senses.whyCN: 当过去的举动并非自己所做，同样的悲伤就变为一种正式的惋惜。

senses.title: A polite refusal
senses.definition: a polite message declining an invitation, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 婉言谢绝邀请，常用复数
senses.example: She sent her regrets and stayed home with the children.
senses.exampleCN: 她致意婉辞，留在家中陪孩子。
senses.why: To decline politely is to wrap a no in sorrow, and the plural regrets becomes the note that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 礼貌地拒绝，就是用歉意包住一个「不」，而复数的 regrets 就是承载它的那张便条。

intro.en: Regret is a northern French word of lamenting; its first element is not the Latin prefix of repetition but the opening of a verb of weeping.
intro.cn: regret 是法国北部一个表「哀叹」的词；它的第一个成分不是拉丁表重复的前缀，而是一个「哭泣」动词的开头。

items.en: Old French regreter meant to bewail or lament, and it is the immediate source of the English word.
items.cn: 古法语 regreter 意为哀叹或悲悼，是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.en: The second element probably comes from a Germanic verb of weeping or greeting with tears.
items.cn: 第二个成分很可能出自一个日耳曼语中表哭泣的动词。

items.en: The re- here strengthens the lament rather than repeating it, so the word means to weep over, not to weep again.
items.cn: 这里的 re- 加强「哀叹」的语气而非重复动作，所以这个词意为「为……悲叹」，不是「再哭一次」。

items.en: English borrowed regret in the sense of sorrow for something past or beyond remedy.
items.cn: 英语借入 regret 时，其义为对已过去或无可挽回之事的悲伤。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the plural regrets had become a polite formula for declining an invitation.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，复数形式 regrets 已成为婉拒邀请的客套说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for sorrow over the past.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一词干构成的词；近义组收表示对过去之事感到悲伤的词。

entries.definition: Feeling or showing regret.
entries.definitionCN: 懊悔的；遗憾的。

entries.definition: Deserving regret.
entries.definitionCN: 令人遗憾的。

entries.definition: Unfortunately.
entries.definitionCN: 遗憾的是。

entries.definition: Deep guilt for a wrong done.
entries.definitionCN: 懊悔；自责。

entries.definition: A feeling of deep sadness.
entries.definitionCN: 悲伤。

entries.definition: Sorrow that turns one from sin.
entries.definitionCN: 悔改；忏悔。

entries.definition: A statement of sorrow for a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 道歉。

normalIntro.en: The word is a backward look that hurts: it names the pain of a past act and the polite sorrow of a refusal.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一次令人疼痛的回望：它命名对过去举动的痛感，也命名婉拒时客气的歉意。

normal.en: Regret doing something means you wish you had not done it.
normal.cn: regret doing something 指希望自己没做过。

normal.en: Regret to inform is the heavy opening of bad news.
normal.cn: regret to inform 是坏消息沉重的开头。

normal.en: Have no regrets means you would do it all again.
normal.cn: have no regrets 指你愿意再来一遍。

normal.en: The past tense doubles the t: regretted and regretting.
normal.cn: 过去式双写 t：regretted 与 regretting。

normal.en: Send one's regrets is to decline politely, not to grieve.
normal.cn: send one's regrets 是礼貌谢绝，不是哀悼。

abstract.en: Regret is memory with a verdict attached.
abstract.cn: 后悔是附带了判决的记忆。

abstract.en: A life without regret may be a life without attention.
abstract.cn: 毫无悔意的人生，也许是毫不用心的人生。

abstract.en: The polite regret is society's way of softening a no.
abstract.cn: 客气的遗憾，是社会把「不」说得柔软的方式。

examples.en: He regretted the words as soon as they left his mouth.
examples.cn: 话一出口他就后悔了。

examples.en: We regret that the museum will close for the winter.
examples.cn: 博物馆冬季将闭馆，我们对此感到遗憾。

examples.en: She sent her regrets and stayed home with the children.
examples.cn: 她致意婉辞，留在家中陪孩子。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（一再）加 gret（哀叹）：一再为过去的事叹息，就是后悔；对无法改变的事叹息，就是遗憾。

root: 古法语 regreter（哀叹、悲悼，第二个成分可能出自日耳曼语表哭泣的动词）→ 英语 regret；re- 在此是加强语气，不是「再次」前缀。同族有 regretful、regrettable、regrettably。

sensesIntro.en: The core is sorrow turned backward; the senses move from regret for one's own act, to sorrow over what cannot change, to a polite refusal.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「转向过去的悲伤」；义项从为自己的举动后悔，到为无法改变之事遗憾，再到礼貌的婉拒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unsent letter taken out of a drawer and put back again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一封没有寄出的信被反复拿起又放回抽屉。

branches.en: words that cannot be recalled

intro.en: A French verb of lamenting enters English whole, and its intensifying prefix is often mistaken for the Latin prefix of repetition.
intro.cn: 一个法语表哀叹的动词整词进入英语，其加强语气的前缀常被误认作拉丁表重复的前缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here: the word is French, with a Germanic element, so only the French and English forms are listed.

definition_en: containing nothing; having no meaning or value; to remove everything from
core_image: 倒空后的瓶子：里面什么都没有
scene: 搬家那天纸箱一个个被搬空。 She emptied the box onto the floor.
sceneCN: 这里 empty 是「倒空」（第 3 个义项：清空容器）；句意是她把箱子里的东西全倒在地板上。图中可辨识物件：纸箱、摊开的衣物、空荡的房间、卷起的胶带。

derivatives.zh: 空虚；空旷
空手的

senses.title: Containing nothing
senses.definition: with nothing inside
senses.definitionCN: 内部没有任何东西。
senses.example: The hall was empty by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时大厅已空无一人。
senses.why: A container without contents gives the concrete starting image.
senses.whyCN: 容器无物即得具体的起点意象。

senses.title: Without meaning or value
senses.definition: lacking real meaning, comfort, or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏真实意义、慰藉或目标。
senses.example: His apology rang empty.
senses.exampleCN: 他的道歉听来空洞。
senses.why: A hollow container promises much but holds nothing, so words and feelings reuse the image.
senses.whyCN: 空壳容器承诺满满却一无所有，言语与情绪便沿用此象。

senses.title: To remove everything from
senses.definition: to take all the contents out of something
senses.definitionCN: 把某物的所有内容取出来。
senses.example: She emptied the box onto the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她把箱子里的东西全倒在地板上。
senses.why: The state becomes an action: making a container empty.
senses.whyCN: 状态转为动作：使容器变空。

intro.en: Empty grew out of an Old English phrase meaning quite free.
intro.cn: empty 出自古英语一个意为「完全空闲」的短语。

items.en: Old English aemtig came from aemetig, meaning at leisure, quite free.
items.cn: 古英语 aemtig 源于 aemetig，意为闲适、完全空出。

items.en: The root aemeti meant ease or leisure in the Germanic family.
items.cn: 词根 aemeti 在日耳曼语族中意为轻松、闲暇。

items.en: Middle English empti shifted the sense from free time to vacant space.
items.cn: 中古英语 empti 把义从空闲时间移向空缺空间。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective and adds the verb and plural noun uses.
items.cn: 现代英语保留形容词并发展动词与复数名词用法。

items.en: Figurative uses about empty promises and empty feelings spread in modern writing.
items.cn: 关于 empty promises 与空虚感的比喻义在现代文本中铺开。

note.en: Two groups: sound neighbors and the nothing-inside field.
note.cn: 两组：音近词与「内部空无」语义场。

intro.en: Empty compounds freely into everyday and idiomatic words.
intro.cn: empty 自由复合出日常与习语词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin-family words carry the formal vacant and void vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族承担正式的 vacant、void 词汇。

items.example: The emptiness of the desert awed us.
items.exampleCN: 沙漠的空旷令我们敬畏。

items.meaning: a space with nothing in it

items.example: She ran on empty for weeks.

definition_zh: 要点；得分；地点；小数点；指向
definition_en: the main idea of what someone says; a unit of score; an exact place or moment; the dot in a decimal number; also to aim or show direction
core_image: 一根手指伸出去停在半空，所有人的视线顺着这条线落到墙上同一个位置
scene: 会议室里的讨论拖了很久，白板上写满潦草的字，有人忽然把笔尖按在其中一个词上。 She tapped the board and made her point in one short sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 point 指「要点」（第 1 个义项：说话人最想让人记住的那一点）；句意为她敲了敲白板，用一句短话把自己的要点说清楚。图中可辨识物件：写满字的白板、按在词上的笔尖、几张转过来的脸。

derivatives.zh: 由 point 加 -ed 构成，义为「尖的；有针对性的」
由 point 加 -er 构成，义为「指示棒；提示；指针」
由 point 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无意义的；没有尖头的」
与 point 同出拉丁语 punctum，义为「准时的」，原指恰好落在某一刻

senses.title: The main idea in what is said
senses.definition: the central idea that a speaker or writer wants to be understood and remembered
senses.definitionCN: 说话人或作者最想让人理解并记住的那个中心意思
senses.example: Her point was that the plan costs far too much.
senses.exampleCN: 她的要点是这个方案花费太高。
senses.why: Latin punctum named the small mark left by a prick, and a mark is exactly what you put beside the one thing that must not be missed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 punctum 指被刺出的小痕，而人们正是用记号标出那件绝不能漏掉的事。

senses.title: A unit of score in a game or test
senses.definition: one of the units by which a game, a contest or an examination is measured
senses.definitionCN: 衡量一场比赛、一次竞赛或一场考试的计量单位
senses.example: He won the final point with a serve down the line.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一记压边线的发球拿下了最后一分。
senses.why: A score was once kept by making a small mark for each success, so the mark itself became the unit of winning.
senses.whyCN: 过去记分就是每得一分画一个小记号，于是记号本身成了计量的单位。

senses.title: A particular place or moment
senses.definition: an exact spot on a map, a body or a scale, or a particular moment in time
senses.definitionCN: 地图、身体或刻度上确切的一处，或时间上特定的某一刻
senses.example: We met at the point where the two roads meet.
senses.exampleCN: 我们约在两条路交汇的那一点见面。
senses.why: A dot fixes a position and nothing else, which is why the same noun can pin down a place on a map and a moment on a timeline.
senses.whyCN: 一个点只固定位置，别的什么也不带，所以同一个名词既能标定地图上的一处，也能标定时间轴上的一刻。

senses.title: The dot in a decimal number
senses.definition: the mark that separates the whole part of a number from its fraction
senses.definitionCN: 把一个数的整数部分与小数部分分开的记号
senses.example: The reading was three point seven metres.
senses.exampleCN: 读数是三点七米。
senses.why: Because the dot is literally a small prick on the page, the mark that splits a decimal simply inherited the name of the mark itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为那个点字面上就是纸上的一个小刺痕，分开整数与小数的记号便直接继承了「记号」这个名字。

senses.title: To aim or show direction
senses.definition: to turn a finger or an object towards something, or to show what is true or likely
senses.definitionCN: 把手指或物体转向某处，或显示出什么是真的、什么是可能发生的
senses.example: The arrow points north along the coastal path.
senses.exampleCN: 箭头指向沿海小路的北面。
senses.why: A pointed finger and a written dot do the same job, both singling out one thing among many, so the noun turned into a verb of directing attention.
senses.whyCN: 伸出的手指与纸上的点做的是同一件事，都是在众多事物里单单挑出一个，于是名词转成了引导注意的动词。

intro.en: Point comes from a Latin word for a prick and the mark it leaves; the dot is the oldest picture behind the score, the argument and the pointing finger.
intro.cn: point 出自拉丁语中表示「刺」的词以及刺出的痕迹；那个小点，就是得分、论点与指路手指背后最古老的画面。

items.en: The verb pungere meant to prick or pierce, the action of a sharp tip against a surface.
items.cn: 动词 pungere 意为刺、扎，是尖锐之物抵住表面的动作。

items.en: Its neuter past participle punctum named the tiny mark or hole left behind, and so came to mean a dot.
items.cn: 它的中性过去分词 punctum 指留下的细微痕迹或小孔，于是有了「点」的意思。

items.en: Old French point carried the dot, but also a stitch, a moment and a item in an argument.
items.cn: 古法语 point 既保留「点」，也指针脚、某一刻以及论述中的一项。

items.en: English took point first for a dot or a sharp end, then for a mark in a game and the chief item of a speech.
items.cn: 英语先以 point 指点状物或尖端，随后指比赛中的记号与讲话里的主要一项。

items.en: Modern English adds the decimal point, the pointing gesture, point of view, and dozens of fixed phrases.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上小数点、指点的动作、point of view 以及大量固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group stays on the Latin prick and its mark; the near-meaning group gathers the dot, the score, the stage and the act of aiming.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语「刺」及其痕迹展开；近义组收点、得分、阶段与瞄准这些意思。

entries.definition: Having a sharp end, or clearly aimed at one person.
entries.definitionCN: 有尖端的；明显针对某一个人的。

entries.definition: A stick, cursor or hint that shows where to look.
entries.definitionCN: 指示棒、光标或提示。

entries.definition: Having no purpose or result at all.
entries.definitionCN: 完全没有目的或结果的。

entries.definition: Arriving exactly at the agreed time.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好在约定时刻到达的。

entries.definition: The marks such as commas and full stops used in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 书写中使用的逗号、句号等标记。

entries.definition: A small round mark.
entries.definitionCN: 小而圆的点。

entries.definition: The number of points won in a game.
entries.definitionCN: 比赛中赢得的分数。

entries.definition: A particular point in a process or development.
entries.definitionCN: 过程或发展中的某一阶段。

entries.definition: To point or direct something at a target.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物对准目标。

normalIntro.en: Everything here grows from one tiny mark made by a sharp tip, and that mark still explains the score, the argument and the finger.
normalIntro.cn: 这里的一切都长自尖端留下的一个小记号，而这个记号至今能解释得分、论点与手指。

normal.en: Pungere means to prick, and punctum is the mark a prick leaves, so every sense starts from a tiny mark.
normal.cn: pungere 意为刺，punctum 是刺出的小痕，所以每个义项都从这一个小记号出发。

normal.en: To point at something is to put an invisible dot on it, which is why the noun became a verb.
normal.cn: 指着某物，等于在它上面放一个看不见的点，名词就这样变成了动词。

normal.en: A point in a game was once a tally mark, so the score and the dot are the same mark seen twice.
normal.cn: 比赛中的一分原本就是一个记数记号，所以得分与点其实是同一个记号的两次现身。

normal.en: The decimal point is a real dot on the page, and it is the oldest physical sense surviving almost unchanged.
normal.cn: 小数点是纸上真实的一点，也是几乎原封不动留存下来的最古老的实指义。

normal.en: Pointless adds -less, without a point, and the metaphor is still visible: something with nothing to aim at.
normal.cn: pointless 加 -less，意为「没有点」，比喻仍然看得见：没有可瞄准之处。

abstract.en: The same mark that measures a game also marks the one sentence worth remembering, which says how close play and argument are.
abstract.cn: 衡量比赛的记号也被用来标出那句值得记住的话，可见游戏与论辩有多近。

abstract.en: A point is a decision about where to stop: a dot chooses a place on a map the way a conclusion chooses a place in an argument.
abstract.cn: 一个点就是决定在哪里停下：圆点在地图上选定一处，正如结论在论述中选定一处。

abstract.en: When someone says you have missed the point, the image is still spatial, as if the meaning had a location you walked past.
abstract.cn: 当有人说你错过了要点，这个说法仍是空间性的，仿佛意义有一个你走过了的位置。

examples.en: Let me make one point before we vote.
examples.cn: 在投票之前，请让我说明一点。

examples.en: She has already scored twenty points this season.
examples.cn: 这个赛季她已经得了二十分。

examples.en: From this point the road climbs steeply.
examples.cn: 从这里开始，路陡然向上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖因特」——手指一剖，直直对着那一个点，不偏不倚。

root: 拉丁语 pungere（刺）→ 过去分词 punctum（刺出的点、记号）→ 古法语 point → 英语 point。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a mark made by a sharp tip; from it come the idea worth marking, the tally of a game, a fixed spot in space or time, the decimal dot and the act of aiming.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是尖端留下的一个记号；由此生出值得标记的意思、比赛的记数、时空中的定点、小数点以及瞄准的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger held out and stopped in mid-air, every eye in the room following the line to one spot on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指伸出后停在半空，满屋的视线都顺着这条线落在墙上同一处。

branches.en: a sentence that makes a long meeting fall into place
branches.cn: 一句话让冗长的会议落到实处

branches.en: a serve landing just inside the line
branches.cn: 一记刚好落在边线内的发球

branches.en: two roads meeting at one exact spot
branches.cn: 两条路交于确切的一点

branches.en: a dot splitting a number in two
branches.cn: 一个点把数字分成两半

branches.en: a finger and a sentence both singling out one thing
branches.cn: 手指与句子都在挑出同一件事

intro.en: A Latin verb of pricking, its participle turned noun, and a French borrowing together supply the whole family of marks and aims.
intro.cn: 一个表示刺的拉丁动词、由分词转成的名词，加上一次法语借入，共同支撑起这整族关于记号与瞄准的词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_en: a spoken or written account of something, especially one given after watching or investigating it
core_image: 一个人把现场看到的事带回总部，摊开记录本一条条讲清楚
scene: 记者在雨里连线直播间，把刚刚发生的车祸报道给全国观众。 The reporter described the crash in a live report from the road.
sceneCN: 这里 report 是「报道；新闻报告」（第 2 个义项：媒体对事件的叙述）；句意：记者在路边直播中描述了这起撞车事故。

derivatives.zh: 记者
据报道
报道文体；新闻报道

senses.title: An account of facts
senses.definition: a spoken or written description of an event or situation, based on observation or study
senses.definitionCN: 基于观察或研究，对事件或情况作出的口头或书面叙述
senses.example: The committee published its report on air quality.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会发布了空气质量报告。
senses.why: The Latin source means to carry back, so the core sense is information brought back from a place or event.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「搬回来」，所以核心义是把某地或某事件的信息带回来。

senses.title: A news story
senses.definition: an article or broadcast that tells the public about a recent event
senses.definitionCN: 向公众讲述近期事件的报道文章或广播节目
senses.example: The evening report led with the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间报道以暴风雨为头条。
senses.why: Journalism turns the carried-back account into a public product, which becomes the news sense.
senses.whyCN: 新闻业把「带回来的叙述」变成面向公众的产品，于是产生新闻报道义。

senses.title: To give an official account
senses.definition: to tell an authority about something that has happened
senses.definitionCN: 向权威机构说明已经发生的事情
senses.example: She reported the theft to the police.
senses.exampleCN: 她向警方报了盗窃案。
senses.why: Reporting is the act of carrying information to someone who needs it, especially an authority.
senses.whyCN: report 就是把信息带给需要它的人，尤其是权威机构。

senses.title: To be accountable to
senses.definition: to be managed by or responsible to a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 受某位上级管理，或对其负责
senses.example: The new assistant reports directly to the director.
senses.exampleCN: 新助理直接向主任汇报。
senses.why: If information must be carried to a superior, then the person doing the carrying is under that superior.
senses.whyCN: 如果信息必须传给上级，那么负责传递的人就处于该上级的管理之下。

intro.en: Report comes from Latin reportare, to carry back, built from re-, back, and portare, to carry.
intro.cn: report 来自拉丁语 reportare（搬回），由 re-（回）与 portare（搬运）构成。

items.en: Portare means to carry, and it is the source of transport and portable.
items.cn: portare 意为搬运，是 transport 与 portable 的来源。

items.en: Reportare adds re-, back, and means to bring news or an answer back.
items.cn: reportare 加上 re-（回），意为把消息或答复带回来。

items.en: Old French reporter keeps the sense of telling what has been learned.
items.cn: 古法语 reporter 保留「讲述所知」的意思。

items.en: Middle English report covers both the telling and the written account.
items.cn: 中古英语 report 既指讲述，也指书面记录。

items.en: Newspapers give report the specialised sense of a news item.
items.cn: 报纸赋予 report「新闻条目」的专门含义。

items.en: Modern English adds the workplace sense of answering to a manager.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了职场中「向管理者汇报」的用法。

note.en: Report is a carrying-back word, and its family includes the person who carries the news and the style of news writing.
note.cn: report 是一个「带回信息」的词，其词族包括带消息的人和新闻写作文体。

entries.definition: a person who gathers and tells news
entries.definitionCN: 记者

entries.definition: according to what people say
entries.definitionCN: 据报道

entries.definition: the style of reporting news in writing
entries.definitionCN: 报道文体

entries.definition: a description of an event
entries.definitionCN: 叙述；描述

entries.definition: something said or written officially
entries.definitionCN: 声明；陈述

entries.definition: a written note of facts kept for the future
entries.definitionCN: 记录；档案

entries.definition: a short official news report
entries.definitionCN: 公告；简报

normalIntro.en: Report contains port, the carrying root of transport, so the memory picture is carrying information back from the scene.
normalIntro.cn: report 含有 port 这个「搬运」词根，也见于 transport，所以记忆画面是从现场把信息搬回来。

normal.en: Re- means back, and port means carry: carry the news back.
normal.cn: re- 表示回，port 表示搬运：把消息搬回来。

normal.en: A reporter is the person who does the carrying.
normal.cn: reporter 就是负责搬运消息的人。

normal.en: Report to your manager means carry information to that manager.
normal.cn: report to your manager 就是把信息带到经理那里。

normal.en: A news report is information carried back to the public.
normal.cn: news report 就是带回给公众的信息。

normal.en: Report a crime is the official version of telling what happened.
normal.cn: report a crime 是「说明发生了什么」的正式说法。

abstract.en: Picture a messenger running from the battlefield back to the camp.
abstract.cn: 想象信使从战场跑回营地。

abstract.en: Imagine a notebook filled at the scene and read aloud in an office.
abstract.cn: 想象在现场写满的笔记本，在办公室里被大声读出来。

abstract.en: Think of a microphone carrying a voice from the street into a studio.
abstract.cn: 想象麦克风把街上的声音送进演播室。

examples.en: The report shows a sharp rise in house prices.
examples.cn: 这份报告显示房价大幅上涨。

examples.en: The theft was reported to the police at once.
examples.cn: 盗窃案立即报了警。

examples.en: She reports to the head of the department.
examples.cn: 她向部门负责人汇报。

dict_mnemonic.text: re-（回）+ port（搬运）＝把消息搬回来，即报告；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）+ portare（搬运）→ reportare（带回消息）→ 古法语 reporter → 中古英语 report。

sensesIntro.en: Information carried back becomes the account, then the published news story, then the act of informing an authority, and finally the line of duty to a manager.
sensesIntro.cn: 被带回的信息先成为叙述，再成为公开的新闻报道，然后是向权威报告的动作，最后是向管理者负责的隶属关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: information carried back from the scene to the people who need it.
core.cn: 核心意象：信息从现场被带回给需要它的人。

branches.en: The account itself is the basic noun sense.
branches.cn: 叙述本身，是最基本的名词义项。

branches.en: Carried-back information becomes a public news story.
branches.cn: 带回的信息变成面向公众的新闻报道。

branches.en: Carrying information to an authority is the official verb.
branches.cn: 把信息带给权威机构，是正式的动词用法。

branches.en: The one who carries information upward is accountable to that superior.
branches.cn: 向上传递信息的人，对那位上级负责。

branches.en: A private account and a public news item share the same content and direction.
branches.cn: 内部叙述与公开新闻共享同样的内容和方向。

intro.en: Report is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin carrying root, with an English noun-and-verb shape.
intro.cn: report 由拉丁前缀与拉丁「搬运」词根构成，在英语中兼作名词和动词。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- means back, and portare means to carry, so reportare is to carry something back.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示回，portare 表示搬运，所以 reportare 就是「把东西搬回来」。

items.example: Re- appears in report and return.
items.exampleCN: re- 出现在 report 与 return 中。

items.example: Portare is the root of report and transport.
items.exampleCN: portare 是 report 与 transport 的词根。
reportare 由 re- 与 portare 合成。
report 保留了「带回」的画面。
reportedly 在 report 后加 -ed 和 -ly。

items.meaningCN: 表示集合或过程的名词词尾

definition_en: more than usual, or more than other things; particularly
core_image: 聚光灯：在一群东西中把一束光打到某个上
scene: 满桌家常菜里，那盘糖醋排骨最先被夹空。 I love this restaurant, especially its sweet and sour ribs.
sceneCN: 这里 especially 是「尤其」（第 1 个义项：突出其中之一）；句意是我爱这家店，尤其爱糖醋排骨。

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀的基础形容词，义为「特别的；专门的」
由 special 加 -ty 构成，义为「专业；特产；招牌菜」
由 special 加 -ist 构成，义为「专家；专科医生」

senses.title: Particularly, more than others
senses.definition: used to single out one person or thing from a group as more notable
senses.definitionCN: 从一群中特别点出某人或某物
senses.example: Everyone was tired, especially the little boy.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都很累，尤其是那个小男孩。
senses.why: Special means set apart, and the -ly adverb points the setting-apart at one member of the group.
senses.whyCN: special 本义是「被单独挑出」，-ly 副词把这种「挑出」指向群体中的某一个。

senses.title: To a great degree
senses.definition: very much, or to an unusual extent, often before adjectives in informal use
senses.definitionCN: 程度很深，口语中常放在形容词前
senses.example: The soup was especially good that day.
senses.exampleCN: 那天这汤格外好喝。
senses.why: A singled-out thing is also lifted above the average, so the word slides into meaning very.
senses.whyCN: 被挑出之物也被抬到平均线之上，于是词义滑向「非常」。

senses.title: For a particular purpose or person
senses.definition: made or done for one special purpose or person
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的或人而做
senses.example: This gift was bought especially for your birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 这份礼物是特意为你的生日买的。
senses.why: When something is set apart for one use, the direction of the setting-apart becomes purpose.
senses.whyCN: 当某物被单独留作一用时，「挑出」的方向就成了目的。

intro.en: Especially comes from special, which traces to Latin species meaning appearance or kind. To be special is to be set apart as its own kind.
intro.cn: especially 由 special 派生，special 上溯拉丁语 species「外形、种类」。special 即「被单独归为一类」。

items.en: Latin species meant 'appearance, look, kind', the visible form by which things are told apart.
items.cn: 拉丁语 species 意为「外形、样子、种类」，是区分事物的可见形式。

items.en: The adjective specialis meant 'of a particular kind, individual', built on the root of species.

items.en: Old French special kept the meaning 'particular, distinctive' in medieval use.
items.cn: 古法语 special 在中世纪沿用「特别的、有区别的」之意。

items.en: English took special in the thirteenth century and formed especially shortly after.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 special，随后不久造出 especially。

abstract.en: Feel the teacher holding up one page among a stack of essays.
abstract.cn: 动作：老师从一摞作文里单独举起一页。

examples.en: I like fruit, especially watermelon in summer.

definition_en: a warning sound or device, or the fear it causes, or to make someone afraid
core_image: 清晨闹钟突然响起来
scene: 清晨，床头的闹钟突然响了起来。 The alarm woke the whole family.
sceneCN: 这里 alarm 是「闹钟」（第 2 个义项：按时叫醒人的钟）；句意为闹钟吵醒了全家。

senses.title: A warning sound
senses.definition: a loud sound that warns of danger
senses.definitionCN: 提醒危险的大声响
senses.example: The fire alarm rang at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 火警警报在中午响了。
senses.why: The Italian cry to arms became a sudden warning sound.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语「拿起武器」的呼喊，变成突然示警的声响。

senses.title: A waking clock
senses.definition: a clock that makes a sound at a set time
senses.definitionCN: 在设定时间发出声响的钟
senses.example: My alarm goes off at six.
senses.exampleCN: 我的闹钟六点响。
senses.why: A clock that warns a sleeper to wake up borrowed the name of the warning.
senses.whyCN: 提醒睡眠者醒来的钟，借用了「示警」的名称。

senses.title: A sudden fear
senses.definition: the fear felt when danger appears
senses.definitionCN: 危险出现时感到的恐惧
senses.example: She jumped up in alarm.
senses.exampleCN: 她惊慌地跳了起来。
senses.why: The warning lands in the mind as fear, which gives the feeling sense.
senses.whyCN: 警报落进心里就成了恐惧，因此有了表示感受的义项。

senses.title: To frighten someone
senses.definition: to make a person feel sudden fear
senses.definitionCN: 使人突然感到害怕
senses.example: The smoke alarmed the neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 烟雾让邻居们惊慌。
senses.why: Putting the warning into other people is the verb sense of making them afraid.
senses.whyCN: 把警报放进别人心里，就是动词「使惊恐」。

items.cn: 法语把这个呼喊缩短为 alarme，意为示警的呼叫。

items.en: English borrowed the word for a sudden call to defend oneself.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪借入这个词，指突然发出的自卫呼叫。

items.en: Later the word named the clock that wakes a sleeper.
items.cn: 后来这个词指叫醒睡眠者的钟。

items.en: Today it covers bells, devices and the fear of danger.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖警铃、装置与对危险的恐惧。

entries.definitionCN: 指多个警报或闹钟。

entries.definition: The past form, meaning made afraid.

entries.definition: It names the object that makes the sound.

definition_zh: 在户外；在露天；户外；露天场所；野外；大自然
definition_en: in or into the open air, outside a building; also the open air itself, especially when thought of as a place to live, work or play
core_image: 帐篷门帘被拉开，人一步跨出去，头顶突然空出一大片
scene: 清晨的营地，帐篷门帘被拉开，有人端着一杯热水走到草地上，抬头看没有屋顶的天空。 She prefers to sleep outdoors whenever the weather allows.
sceneCN: 这里是「在户外、在露天」（第 1 个义项：在建筑物外面）；句意为只要天气允许，她更愿意睡在露天。图中可辨识物件：帐篷门帘、草地、热水杯。

pos.zh: 户外；露天场所；野外；大自然

derivatives.zh: 由 out 与 door 复合、再加 -s 构成副词；outdoor 是它的形容词形式，义为「户外的；露天的」
由 outdoors 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「喜爱户外活动的；适合户外的」
由旧短语 out of doors 连写而成，义为「在户外」，是 outdoors 的另一种写法

senses.title: Outside a building, in the open air
senses.definition: in or into the open air, on the far side of a door or wall rather than inside a building
senses.definitionCN: 在或进入建筑物之外的露天环境，也就是在门或墙的另一侧，而不是在屋里
senses.example: The children played outdoors until the light faded.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在户外玩到天光暗下来。
senses.why: The word is a compressed phrase: out of doors once meant literally passing through the door to the space beyond it, so the adverb still carries a step from inside to outside.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是短语压缩来的：out of doors 原意是「走出门去、到门外的空间」，所以这个副词到今天还带着从室内跨到室外的那一步。

senses.title: The open air as a place to be
senses.definition: the open air, thought of as a place where people spend time, work or rest, as in the outdoors
senses.definitionCN: 把露天的空气当作一个可以待着、干活或休息的地方，如 the outdoors
senses.example: After a week at a desk, he needed the outdoors.
senses.exampleCN: 在桌前坐了一周之后，他需要到户外去。
senses.why: Once the adverb had named the space beyond the door, English could put the definite article in front of it and treat that space as a place with a name, which is how the noun appeared.
senses.whyCN: 副词先给门外那片空间起了名，英语再在它前面加上定冠词，把那片空间当成一个有名字的地方，名词用法就是这样长出来的。

senses.title: Wild open country
senses.definition: open country with woods, hills or water, far from buildings, especially as a place for recreation
senses.definitionCN: 远离建筑的田野、树林、山岭或水域，尤指供人游玩休憩的开阔地带
senses.example: They spent the holiday exploring the great outdoors.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这个假期用来探索广阔的大自然。
senses.why: The phrase the great outdoors added great to the same noun and pushed the meaning from any open air toward wide, unbuilt land, where the absence of roofs becomes the whole attraction.
senses.whyCN: the great outdoors 在同一个名词前加了 great，把意思从「任何露天的空气」推向开阔、没有建筑的土地；在那里，屋顶的缺席本身成了全部吸引力。

intro.en: Outdoors began as the phrase out of doors, a plain description of going through a door into the open, and the modern spelling fuses those words into one adverb and noun.
intro.cn: outdoors 起初是短语 out of doors，平平常常地描述「出了门到露天去」，现代拼写把这几个词粘成了一个副词和一个名词。

items.en: Old English had duru for a door and ūt for out, the two plain words that the later phrase would join.
items.cn: 古英语用 duru 表示门、用 ūt 表示向外，这两个平常的词后来被拼进同一个短语。

items.en: Middle English said out of dores, literally out of the doors, for leaving a house for the open air.
items.cn: 中古英语说 out of dores，字面就是「出了那些门」，用来表示离开屋子到露天去。

items.en: Writers began to set the phrase down as one word, outdoors, and to use it as an adverb of place.
items.cn: 到了十六、十七世纪，作者们把这个短语写成一个词 outdoors，用作表示地点的副词。

items.en: The fused form took a definite article and became a noun, the outdoors, naming the open air as a place rather than a direction.
items.cn: 这个合成形式带上定冠词，成了名词 the outdoors，把露天的空气当作一个地方来指，而不是一个方向。

items.en: Modern English adds the fixed phrase the great outdoors and uses the word for camping, sport and open-air work.
items.cn: 现代英语又添出固定说法 the great outdoors，并用这个词谈露营、运动和露天工作。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the door word and the forms built on the same compound; the near-meaning group collects other names for the air and land outside buildings.
note.cn: 形近组收表示门的词以及由同一复合结构长出的形式；近义组收其他表示「建筑物之外的空气与土地」的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective form, placed before a noun for things done or used in the open air.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，放在名词前，指在露天进行或使用的事物。

entries.definition: Fond of outdoor activities and comfortable in the open air.
entries.definitionCN: 喜爱户外活动、在露天也自在的。

entries.definition: The older phrase from which the single word was formed, meaning outside a house.
entries.definitionCN: 合成词所由来的旧短语，意为在屋子外面。

entries.definition: Used for things inside a building, the reverse of outdoor.
entries.definitionCN: 指建筑物内部的事物，与 outdoor 相对。

entries.definition: The space outside buildings, with no roof above it.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物之外、头顶没有遮蔽的空间；露天。

entries.definition: Land away from towns, with fields, woods and small villages.
entries.definitionCN: 远离城镇、有田野树林与村庄的土地；乡下。

entries.definition: The physical world of plants, animals, weather and landscape.
entries.definitionCN: 植物、动物、天气与地貌构成的物质世界；大自然。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic compound of out and door, so the mnemonics keep the picture of stepping through a doorway into open air.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 out 与 door 的日耳曼语复合，所以联想都围绕「穿过一道门、走进露天」的画面。

normal.en: Outdoors is out of doors compressed, and the door is still visible inside the modern spelling.
normal.cn: outdoors 是 out of doors 压缩来的，那扇门在现代拼写里仍看得见。

normal.en: The plural doors is a fossil of the older phrase out of dores, kept even after the words fused.
normal.cn: 复数 doors 是旧短语 out of dores 留下的化石，词粘成一个以后它也没消失。

normal.en: Outdoor is the adjective; outdoors is the adverb and the noun.
normal.cn: outdoor 是形容词，outdoors 是副词兼名词。

normal.en: Outdoorsy adds -y and describes a person who likes being in the open air.
normal.cn: outdoorsy 加 -y，形容喜欢待在露天的人。

normal.en: The great outdoors uses the definite article to turn open air into a named place.
normal.cn: the great outdoors 用定冠词，把露天的空气变成一个有名字的地方。

abstract.en: A hand pushing a door open and a foot landing on grass.
abstract.cn: 一只手推开门，一只脚落在草上。

abstract.en: The word keeps a door inside it, which is why the open air still feels like something you pass through.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一扇门留在里面，所以露天总像是你必须穿过什么才到得了。

abstract.en: A roof is what the word leaves behind, and that absence is the whole point.
abstract.cn: 屋顶是这个单词留在身后的东西，而这份缺席正是它的全部意思。

examples.en: After a week at a desk, he needed the outdoors.
examples.cn: 在桌前坐了一周之后，他需要到户外去。

examples.en: They spent the holiday exploring the great outdoors.
examples.cn: 他们把这个假期用来探索广阔的大自然。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凹特道兹」——走到门外那片地上，头顶一下就空了；记住 outdoors 是户外。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the space on the far side of a door; the adverb names being there, and the noun names the place itself, first any open air and then wide wild country.

definition_en: a story, especially one that may not be true or is told in an imaginative way
core_image: 炉火边讲述的漫长故事：真假难辨，却让人一直听下去
scene: 祖父在冬夜里讲起年轻时航海遇险的经历，孩子们听得入了迷。 The old sailor told a long tale about his voyage across the stormy sea.
sceneCN: 这里 tale 是「故事、叙述」（第 1 个义项：一段讲述出来的故事）；句意是老水手讲述了一段关于自己跨越风暴之海的漫长故事。

senses.title: A story that someone tells
senses.definition: a story that someone tells, often one that is imaginative or entertaining
senses.definitionCN: 某人讲述的一段故事，常带有想象色彩或趣味性
senses.example: Grandmother told us a tale about a clever fox.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母给我们讲了一只聪明狐狸的故事。
senses.why: The core image is someone narrating by the fire: words flow forward and carry listeners into another world.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是有人在炉边开口叙述：话语向前流淌，把听众带进另一个世界，所以最基本义就是「讲出来的故事」。

senses.title: An account of events, real or invented
senses.definition: an account of a series of events, whether true or invented
senses.definitionCN: 对一连串事件的记述，可以是真实的也可以是虚构的
senses.example: The survivor gave a moving tale of the shipwreck.
senses.exampleCN: 幸存者讲述了感人的沉船经历。
senses.why: A narration may carry real experience; the same flowing words can recount actual events, extending the story sense to personal accounts.
senses.whyCN: 叙述既可以承载虚构，也可以承载真实经历：同一股「流淌的话语」被用来记述事件，于是故事义延伸为「经历、记述」。

senses.title: A lie or an unreliable report
senses.definition: a statement or report that is not true or cannot be trusted
senses.definitionCN: 不真实或不可信的说法、传闻
senses.example: Don't believe that tale; it is just gossip.
senses.exampleCN: 别信那种说法，那只是谣言。
senses.why: Because many fireside stories are invented, the word picked up a hint of fabrication, giving the negative sense of untrustworthy talk.
senses.whyCN: 因为炉边故事常是编出来的，这个词沾上了「虚构」的意味，于是引申出「不实之词、谣言」的贬义。

senses.title: A full reveal of past behavior
senses.definition: the whole story that past marks or evidence reveal about someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 痕迹或证据所揭示出的全部情况
senses.example: The worn boots told their own tale of hard travel.
senses.exampleCN: 磨破的靴子诉说着艰苦旅行的经历。
senses.why: Traces speak like a narrator: marks on an object reveal the past just as words tell a story, so evidence itself becomes a tale.
senses.whyCN: 痕迹会像叙述者一样「开口」：物品上的印记揭示过去，正如话语讲述故事，因此证据本身也成了一种「故事」。

senses.title: A traditional legend passed down
senses.titleCN: 传说；口口相传的古老故事
senses.definition: an old story about past people or events that is passed down by word of mouth
senses.definitionCN: 关于过去人物或事件、经口耳相传保留下来的古老故事
senses.example: The village keeps an ancient tale of a hidden treasure.
senses.exampleCN: 村子保留着一个关于宝藏的古老传说。
senses.why: Fireside narration repeats across generations; when the same story travels through many mouths, it hardens into legend.
senses.whyCN: 炉边叙述代代重复：当同一个故事经过无数张嘴流传下来，它就凝固成了「传说」。

senses.title: A long, tedious amount of talk or writing
senses.definition: a long and often boring piece of speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 冗长且常令人生厌的一大段话语或文字
senses.example: He launched into a long tale about his troubles.
senses.exampleCN: 他开始絮絮叨叨地大讲自己的麻烦。
senses.why: The flowing narration can go on and on; when words keep flowing without end, the story becomes tedious length.
senses.whyCN: 叙述可以不断向前流淌：当话语流个不停、没有尽头时，「故事」就变成了「冗长的讲述」。

senses.title: A tale as a literary genre
senses.definition: a work of fiction, especially a short narrative in literary form
senses.definitionCN: 一种叙事性文学作品，尤指短篇故事
senses.example: The book contains six tales of the Middle Ages.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书收录了六个中世纪故事。
senses.why: Spoken stories were later written down and shaped into art; the narration itself became a named literary genre.
senses.whyCN: 口头故事后来被写定并打磨成艺术：叙述本身成为一种有名字的文学体裁，即「故事体作品」。

senses.title: Dead men tell no tales as a saying
senses.titleCN: 谚语用法：死人不会泄密
senses.definition: used in the saying that dead people cannot reveal secrets
senses.definitionCN: 用于谚语，指死去的人不会泄露秘密
senses.example: They silenced the witness, saying dead men tell no tales.
senses.exampleCN: 他们让证人闭了嘴，说死人不会泄密。
senses.why: A tale can reveal what someone knows; when the narrator is gone, the flow of words stops, so secrets stay buried.
senses.whyCN: 故事能泄露讲述者所知的事：叙述者一旦不在，话语之流便停止，秘密也就被埋葬。

intro.en: Tale comes from Old English, sharing a deep root with the verb tell, and its history runs through Germanic storytelling traditions.
intro.cn: tale 源自古英语，与动词 tell 同出一个深层词根，其历史贯穿日耳曼的口述传统。

items.en: The root is generally reconstructed as *talō in Proto-Germanic, connected with counting and speaking, from the idea of counting out words.
items.cn: 该词根一般重构为原始日耳曼语 *talō，与「数、说」相关，来自「数出话语」的观念。

items.en: Old English talu meant tale, speech, and also counting; the same root gave the verb tell, which once meant both to count and to narrate.
items.cn: 古英语 talu 意为故事、言语，也指计数；同一词根派生出动词 tell，后者一度兼指「数数」与「讲述」。

items.en: In Middle English the spelling tale settled, and the counting sense separated into the word tale replaced by number talk and new borrowings.
items.cn: 中古英语时期拼写定型为 tale，「计数」义逐渐分离，讲述义成为主导。

items.en: Chaucer's Canterbury Tales fixed the word as the standard term for a told narrative in English literary tradition.
items.cn: 乔叟的《坎特伯雷故事集》使 tale 成为英语文学传统中「讲述的叙事」的标准用词。

items.en: Today tale suggests an old-fashioned or imaginative story, often with a hint that it may not be fully true.
items.cn: 现代英语中 tale 多指老式或富于想象的故事，常带「未必全真」的意味。

note.en: Tale is easily confused with similar-looking nouns and with near-meaning story words.
note.cn: tale 容易与拼写相近的名词以及近义的故事类词汇混淆。

senses.title: The back part of the foot
senses.definition: the rounded back part of the foot
senses.definitionCN: 脚掌后端的圆状部分
senses.example: His heel hurt after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 走了很长的路后，他的脚后跟疼。
senses.why: The foot ends in a rounded pad at the back, and the word names that pad directly.
senses.whyCN: 脚掌末端有个圆形的后垫，这个词直接命名这个部位。

senses.title: The back part of a shoe
senses.definition: the part of a shoe that supports the heel of the foot

senses.example: She bought a pair of shoes with low heels.

items.en: In Middle English, heel extended to the back part of shoes and stockings.

items.en: Modern English added idioms like Achilles' heel and head over heels.

与 passage 同出拉丁语 passus（一步）与俗拉丁语 passare，是这一族词的基础动词，义为「经过；通过」
由 pass 加 -er 与 by 复合而成，义为「路过的人；行人」

senses.title: A short section of a text or a piece of music
senses.definition: a short part of a book, poem, speech or piece of music, considered on its own
senses.definitionCN: 书、诗、演讲或乐曲中单独拿出来看的一小部分
senses.example: She read the passage aloud to the class.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这一段朗读给全班听。
senses.why: Passage first meant the act of going through, so a stretch of writing is pictured as a stretch of road that a reader travels from one end to the other.
senses.whyCN: passage 最早指「穿过去」这个动作，所以一段文字被想成一段路，读者从这头走到那头。

senses.title: A narrow way through or along something
senses.definition: a narrow way that lets a person move through a building, between walls or along a corridor
senses.definitionCN: 让人穿过建筑、墙与墙之间或沿走廊行走的窄路
senses.example: A narrow passage led from the street into a quiet courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 一条窄通道从街道通向安静的院子。
senses.why: The word names the act of passing, and the place that makes passing possible borrows the same name: a passage is where the going-through happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指「通过」这个动作，而让通过成为可能的那段空间就借用了同一个名字：passage 就是「穿过去」发生的地方。

senses.title: A journey, especially by sea or air
senses.definition: a journey from one place to another, especially by ship, and also the fare paid for it
senses.definitionCN: 从一地到另一地的行程，尤指乘船，也指为此支付的船费
senses.example: The storm made the passage across the channel dangerous.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴使横渡海峡的航程变得危险。
senses.why: A voyage is simply a long act of passing from one shore to another, so the noun for going through extends to the whole crossing and to the money it costs.
senses.whyCN: 一次航行不过是从一片岸到另一片岸的漫长「穿过」，于是表示穿过的名词扩展到整段渡海行程，以及为它付出的钱。

senses.title: The process of a law being approved, or of time going by
senses.definition: the formal approval of a law by a legislature, or the movement of time from one moment to the next
senses.definitionCN: 立法机构对法律的正式通过，或时间从一刻走向下一刻
senses.example: The passage of the new law took almost a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这项新法几乎花了一年才通过。
senses.why: A bill must go through a series of stages before it becomes law, and time goes through the hours in the same way, so both are described with the noun of passing.
senses.whyCN: 一项法案必须走过一连串阶段才能成为法律，时间也同样一小时一小时地走过去，所以两者都用这个表示「通过」的名词。

intro.en: Passage goes back to Latin passus, a step, and the verb passare, to walk or cross, which French turned into passer and then into the noun passage.
intro.cn: passage 上溯拉丁语 passus（一步）与动词 passare（走、穿过），法语把它变成 passer，又造出名词 passage。

items.en: Pandere meant to spread or stretch out, and a leg stretched forward gives the family its first picture of movement.
items.cn: pandere 意为展开、伸开，一条腿向前伸出，给了这一族词最初的移动画面。

items.en: Passus named a single step and also a fixed length of ground measured in steps.
items.cn: passus 指单独的一步，也指以步为单位量出的固定长度。

items.en: The everyday verb passare meant to walk, to cross or to go through, and it is the source of the French verb.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语的动词 passare 意为走、越过、穿过，是法语动词的来源。

items.en: Old French made the noun passage for a crossing, a way through and a section of a text.
items.cn: 古法语造出名词 passage，指渡海、穿行的路，以及文本中的一段。

items.en: English borrowed passage in the thirteenth century and kept all three strands: the act of going through, the way itself, and a stretch of writing.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 passage，并保留了三条线索：通过的动作、通过的路，以及一段文字。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin step or merely spelled alike; the near-meaning group collects words for a way through and for a slice of a text.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个拉丁语「步」之上或只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示通道与文本片段的词。

entries.definition: To go past or through something, or a document that lets you travel.
entries.definitionCN: 经过或穿过某物，也指准许通行的证件。

entries.definition: A corridor or narrow way that connects two places.
entries.definitionCN: 连接两处的走廊或窄路。

entries.definition: A person travelling in a vehicle; only the spelling is close, the sense is different.
entries.definitionCN: 乘车、乘船或乘飞机的人；只是拼写相近，词义不同。

entries.definition: A very strong feeling or a deep enthusiasm; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的情感或深切的爱好；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A long narrow space inside a building with doors on both sides.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑内部两侧有门的长窄空间；走廊。

entries.definition: A short piece taken from a book, film or piece of music.
entries.definitionCN: 从书、电影或乐曲中摘出的一小段。

entries.definition: A journey across water, or a place where a road or line can be crossed.
entries.definitionCN: 渡过水面的行程，或可以横穿的地方。

entries.definition: A short passage taken out of a longer text.
entries.definitionCN: 从较长文字中摘出的一段。

normalIntro.en: Passage keeps the picture of a step forward, and every sense is something a step can do: cross a room, cross a sea, cross a page, or carry a law to its end.
normalIntro.cn: passage 始终保留「向前一步」的画面，每个义项都是步子能做的事：穿过房间、穿过海面、穿过书页，或者把一项法案走到终点。

normal.en: Passage is pass plus the French ending -age, so the word says the act of passing before it says any place or text.
normal.cn: passage 是 pass 加法语词尾 -age，所以这个词先说的是「通过」这个动作，其次才是某处地方或某段文字。

normal.en: A passage in a building and a passage in a book share the idea of a stretch you travel along from one end to the other.
normal.cn: 建筑里的通道与书里的一段共享同一个想法：一段可以从头走到尾的路程。

normal.en: The passage of time and the passage of a bill both describe something moving through stages until it arrives.
normal.cn: 时间的流逝与法案的通过，都描述某物穿过一个个阶段，直到抵达终点。

normal.en: Passage is not the same as passenger: the first is the way or the trip, the second is the person carried along it.
normal.cn: passage 与 passenger 不同：前者是路或行程，后者是被带着走完这段路的人。

normal.en: Passion looks almost identical but comes from a Latin word for suffering, so the shared spelling is a coincidence of history.
normal.cn: passion 看起来几乎一样，却来自拉丁语中表示「受苦」的词，所以相同的拼写只是历史造成的巧合。

abstract.en: A single word for a corridor, a sea trip and a paragraph tells us that reading is also a kind of travel.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时指走廊、海上行程与段落，说明阅读本身也是一种旅行。

abstract.en: A law passes the way a person passes a gate: it must be let through stage by stage, and each stage can stop it.
abstract.cn: 法律通过就像人过一道门：必须一关一关被放行，而每一关都可能把它拦下。

abstract.en: The passage of time is the one journey nobody can refuse, which is why the word sounds calm even when it describes loss.
abstract.cn: 时间的流逝是无人能拒绝的一段行程，所以这个词即使在说失去时，听上去也很平静。

core.cn: 核心意象：一条窄廊从两堵石墙之间穿过，尽头透出一线光。

intro.en: The word joins a Latin noun for a step, a Latin verb for crossing, and a French noun ending that names an action or its result.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语表示「一步」的名词、表示「穿过」的动词，以及法语中表示动作或结果的名词词尾拼在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin passus and passare are both recorded, so the ancestry of passage is reliable as far as the French stage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 passus 与 passare 均有记录，因此 passage 的世系直到法语阶段都是可靠的。

definition_en: to put a question, or to request something, or to invite someone
core_image: 工作人员抬头询问来人的名字
scene: 登记处，工作人员抬起头问来人的名字。 She asked me my name.

senses.title: To put a question
senses.definition: to say a question in order to get an answer
senses.definitionCN: 说出问题以得到答复
senses.example: She asked me my name.
senses.exampleCN: 她问了我的名字。
senses.why: The old verb meant to seek out, so going to someone for an answer is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 古动词意为寻问，所以走向某人求答复就是第一义。

senses.title: To request something
senses.definition: to say that you want something to be given or done
senses.definitionCN: 说出希望得到某物或做成某事
senses.example: He asked for a glass of water.
senses.exampleCN: 他要了一杯水。
senses.why: The seeking turns into a request when what is wanted is a thing rather than an answer.
senses.whyCN: 当所求的是一件东西而不是答复，寻问就变成请求。

senses.title: To invite someone
senses.definition: to invite a person to come somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 请某人到某处
senses.example: They asked us to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他们邀请我们参加聚会。
senses.why: Inviting is asking a person to be present, so the same verb covers it.
senses.whyCN: 邀请就是请一个人到场，所以同一个动词也能表示。

items.cn: 中古英语保留它，指提出问题。

items.en: Later it also covered asking for a thing.
items.cn: 后来它也指索要某件东西。

items.en: Today it also means to invite someone.
items.cn: 今天它也指邀请某人。

senses.title: At low speed
